title: Stack [Push & Pop]
description:
## The Stack
The stack is a region of memory that grows downward. You interact with it using two instructions:

- `push rax` - saves rax onto the stack (rsp decreases by 8)
- `pop rax` - restores the top value into rax (rsp increases by 8)

It's last-in, first-out (LIFO) - like a stack of plates.
```asm
mov rax, 42
push rax        ; stack: [42]
mov rax, 99
push rax        ; stack: [99, 42]
pop rbx         ; rbx = 99, stack: [42]
pop rcx         ; rcx = 42, stack: []
```

The stack is how you save registers when you need them later - especially before a `syscall` which destroys `rcx` and `r11`.

**Use the Step button and watch the Stack tab to see values appear and disappear!**

---
## Assignment:
Push the values 10, 20, and 30 onto the stack, then pop them into `rax`, `rbx`, and `rcx`. Print the message to confirm it worked. Step through and watch the stack!
starterCode:
section .data
    msg db "Stack works!", 10
    len equ $ - msg

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    ; push 10, 20, 30
    ; pop into rax, rbx, rcx

    ; print
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall

    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
